saturationDecisions.why: at gate (3) but a changed path is on its surface

themes.theme: the constrained generation gate prices only (n, k) and ignores the constraint set, so validate admits inputs whose real cost is several times the budget's documented ceiling
findingSummaries: `constrainedWork(n, k) = n*n*min(k, n-1)` is the only quantity `validate` / `checkWellFormed` compare against `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK`, and it has no term for the constraint set even though `validateDetailed` holds `cons` when it calls it. Every legality decision in the generator (`legalEdge`, `swapJoin`, `forceConnect`) is a `cons.isProhibited` probe — a template-string build plus a lookup in the prohibited `Set` — whose unit cost rises sharply with the size of that Set. The result is that a SPARSE roster sitting exactly at the work budget can cost several times the calibrated worst case, and `validate` returns `[]` for it. The gate itself is on the same curve: `validateDetailed` materialises every pair array (`pairsOf`) several times and then runs the O(n^2) `connectivityReasons` walk, all with the same per-probe penalty.
themes.remediation: Give the estimator the constraint set it is already handed: change `constrainedWork(n, k)` to `constrainedWork(n, k, cons)` (or add a separate `constraintWork` term) so the compared quantity includes `cons.prohibitedCount` — the generator performs O(n) prohibited probes per edge added plus O(n^2) in `connectivityReasons`, so a term such as `n*n*min(k,n-1) + PROBE_COST * cons.prohibitedCount` is the right shape. Recalibrate `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK` against the dense-prohibition shape rather than only the near-complete-k corner, mirror the new term in `reference-python`, and keep `validateDetailed` and `constrainedGreedy`'s `checkWellFormed` calling the same function so the refusal and the throw stay in step. Update the ceiling figures in the `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK` docblock and in `lib/CLAUDE.md`'s "Generation cost scales as n^2*min(k,n-1)" note, which states the same (n, k)-only model.

gating.failure:
Measured on this machine, all at n=5000, k=4, i.e. `constrainedWork` = 1e8 = exactly `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK`, all with `validate(cons, 4)` returning `[]` (repro: /home/user/ringweave/.review-scratch/dos-probe/p8.mjs and p9.mjs):
  prohibitedCount = 0        -> validate ~0 ms,     constrainedGreedy 16.5 s
  prohibitedCount = 1e6      -> validate 0.77 s,    constrainedGreedy 52.9 s
  prohibitedCount = 5e6      -> validate 4.5 s,     constrainedGreedy 60.5 s
  prohibitedCount = 9e6      -> validate 15.2 s,    constrainedGreedy 91.5 s
End-to-end through the safe entry point: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(5000, 4, cons)` with 5e6 prohibited pairs returns after 81.4 s with `report.refusals.length === 0`. `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK`'s own docblock states the budget "hold[s] worst-case generation to ~13 s for sparse rosters and ~46 s at the deepest allowed corner (n~464, k=n-1)" — this is a sparse roster (k=4) exceeding both, by 2x at 9e6 pairs, and 15 s of that is spent inside the gate that is supposed to refuse it. A dense-prohibition block layout reproduces the same effect at lower n (p7.mjs: n=3000, k=4, 4.46e6 pairs -> 19.1 s at a modelled work of 3.6e7, a rate of 1.9e6 units/s, below the 2.2e6/s figure the constant is calibrated on). Present-day reachability: this is via the library's public API only — `app/src/constraints.ts` caps stored pairs at `MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS = 200` and the app's n at 1000, so the shipping UI cannot reach it today; the amplification is also a bounded constant factor (prohibitedCount <= n(n-1)/2), not an unbounded hang. It is a calibration hole in the library's stated authoritative gate, not a live app DoS.
gating.remediation: Give the estimator the constraint set it is already handed: change `constrainedWork(n, k)` to `constrainedWork(n, k, cons)` (or add a separate `constraintWork` term) so the compared quantity includes `cons.prohibitedCount` — the generator performs O(n) prohibited probes per edge added plus O(n^2) in `connectivityReasons`, so a term such as `n*n*min(k,n-1) + PROBE_COST * cons.prohibitedCount` is the right shape. Recalibrate `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK` against the dense-prohibition shape rather than only the near-complete-k corner, mirror the new term in `reference-python`, and keep `validateDetailed` and `constrainedGreedy`'s `checkWellFormed` calling the same function so the refusal and the throw stay in step. Update the ceiling figures in the `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK` docblock and in `lib/CLAUDE.md`'s "Generation cost scales as n^2*min(k,n-1)" note, which states the same (n, k)-only model.
gating.invariant: For every `(n, k, cons)` for which `validate(cons, k)` returns `[]`, the cost estimate compared against `MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK` must be non-decreasing in the constraint set: for any `cons1` whose required/prohibited/prior sets are subsets of `cons2`'s at the same `n`, `estimate(n, k, cons1) <= estimate(n, k, cons2)`, and `validate` must refuse whenever `estimate > MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK`. Equivalently: adding prohibited pairs to an admitted input can only ever move it toward refusal, never leave it admitted at an unchanged estimate — so no input dimension the generator's inner loop probes is invisible to the gate.
